title: Democrats win control of the US House and Senate in the 2026 midterms
seoTitle: US midterm results 2026: Democrats win Congress
dek: Democrats have at least 54 Senate seats and a House majority that NBC News projects at 258 or more. Senate races in Mississippi and Alaska are still being counted.
happened: In the 3 November elections, the Associated Press called the Senate for Democrats shortly before midnight and the House at about 1:25 a.m. on 4 November. Democrats have at least 54 Senate seats to 44 for Republicans after flipping seven: Iowa, Kansas, Maine, North Carolina, Ohio, South Carolina and Texas. In the House, NBC News projected at least 258 Democratic seats and CBS News estimated 251 to 268; 42 House races were still uncalled on 4 November. Before the vote, Republicans held the House 218 to 214 and the Senate 53 to 47. Democrats also flipped five governorships: Georgia, Iowa, Nevada, Ohio and Texas. Among ballot measures, Nevada approved abortion rights and voter ID, and Idaho rejected an abortion-rights measure.

sides.says: He told Fox News he was "a little bit surprised" and "thought we'd do better", and said: "I don't view it as a hit on me." On Truth Social he wrote: "I wasn't on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!" He said he would accept the results and work with Democrats, but would veto what they pass.

Vice President JD Vance wrote: "The reason we lost is the war", meaning the war with Iran. House Speaker Mike Johnson told staffers he will not seek another term as Republican leader and pledged a "firewall of House Republicans". Senate Majority Leader John Thune said "Senate Republicans will not stand idly by" as Democrats try to undo Republican policies.

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries called the result an "American tsunami" and has launched his bid to become Speaker. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer told Americans "Relief is on the way" and said he will seek to become majority leader again. Democrats plan hearings, document requests and subpoenas on the Trump administration; major laws would still need the president's signature.

next: Mississippi: Democrat Scott Colom led Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith by 1,138 votes with 96% counted on Wednesday night. Mail ballots count if they arrive by 5 p.m. on 10 November and counties must submit certified results by 13 November; the state has no automatic recount, so a challenge would go through the courts. Alaska: Democrat Mary Peltola led Sen. Dan Sullivan by 637 votes with nearly a quarter of the votes uncounted; ranked-choice results are not due until 18 November. The new Congress convenes on 3 January.
summary: Democrats won both chambers of the US Congress in the 3 November midterms, taking the House and flipping seven Senate seats. They have at least 54 senators, and two more Republican-held seats, Mississippi and Alaska, are still undecided with Democrats narrowly ahead in the count. NBC News projects at least 258 House seats for Democrats; CBS News estimates 251 to 268. They also flipped five governorships. President Trump says the result was not a verdict on him; Vice President Vance blames the war with Iran. Democrats take over when the new Congress convenes on 3 January, and President Trump keeps his veto.

conflicts: House seat figures are projections and differ by newsroom: NBC News says at least 258 for Democrats, CBS News 251 to 268.
The Mississippi margin moved during the count: NBC News reported Colom ahead by 65 votes on Wednesday afternoon; AP figures cited by Al Jazeera and Time gave 1,138 that night.
